title: Atom Forge
summary: Drag protons, neutrons and electrons into nuclei and shells to forge elements mission by mission.
mobileSupportNote: Stacked vertical-scroll layout works end-to-end at 390x844 (steppers and tap-a-token are the primary paths; pointer drag works but drop targets are compact below 480px).

cover.alt: Atom Forge mid-mission on the Carbon Core mission: a Swiss scientific-poster workbench with the atom canvas centre-right — six orange protons and six grey neutrons packed in the nucleus, shell 1 sealed at 2/2 electrons and shell 2 holding 3 of 8 ultramarine electrons. The left readout names the element Carbon with counters Z 6, N 6, electrons 5, mass 12, charge +1, and an orange forge note explains the missing sixth electron; the periodic strip at the foot shows H, He and Li stamped ultramarine with the carbon target outlined in orange.

desktop.alt: The Atom Forge mission ledger at 1440x900: a poster-style index of twelve mission rows (First Spark, Seal the First Shell, up to Calcium, Bone Builder) on warm off-white paper with hairline rules, mono isotope notations and FORGED/OPEN/LOCKED status stamps — mission 01 is open, the rest locked; a progress counter reads 0/12 and the periodic mini-strip of the first 20 elements runs along the foot.

tablet.alt: The atom builder at 1024x768, the hero viewport: Mission 01 First Spark is open with one orange proton in the nucleus and no electrons yet — the readout identifies Hydrogen with charge +1 and an orange note asking for one electron. Canvas, live counters, zone steppers (48px) and the three-token particle tray dock all fit the screen without scrolling.

mobile.alt: The same First Spark bench stacked vertically at 390x844: mission brief and target on top, the Hydrogen readout with counters, the atom canvas with its single proton, zone steppers, the horizontal three-token particle tray, and the periodic strip of 20 element tiles below.
